skills.name: Function notation

steps.a: read f(x) aloud and in meaning

skills.wrong_turn: f(x) is not f times x. f(2) means "the output at 2", not 2f.
skills.rule: f(x) is read "f of x": the output of f when the input is x.

skills.name: Evaluate functions

steps.d: evaluate from a graph or table

skills.wrong_turn: f(−2) for x² is (−2)² = 4, not −2² = −4. Put negatives in parentheses.
skills.rule: To evaluate f(a), replace every x with (a) and simplify.

skills.name: Domain & range
skills.wrong_turn: The range isn't everything on the y-axis. f(x) = x² never outputs negatives, so its range is y ≥ 0.
skills.rule: Domain: all allowed inputs. Range: all outputs that actually occur.

skills.name: Reading function graphs

steps.b: solve f(x) = k on a graph

skills.wrong_turn: To solve f(x) = 3 on a graph, look for height 3 and read the x-values. Don't go to x = 3.
skills.rule: f(a) is the height of the graph above x=a.

skills.name: Functions in context
skills.wrong_turn: C(10) = 25 doesn't mean 10 dollars buy 25 rides. Input first: 10 rides cost 25 dollars.
skills.rule: f(a)=b means: when the input is a (in its units), the output is b (in its units).

skills.name: Average rate of change
skills.wrong_turn: Divide by the change in input, not the change in output: from (1, 1) to (4, 16) it's 15/3, not 3/15.

skills.name: Increasing & decreasing

steps.d: connect to sign of rate of change

skills.wrong_turn: Intervals of increase are x-values, not y-values. For x², write (0, ∞), not "from y = 0 up".
skills.rule: f is increasing on an interval if bigger inputs give bigger outputs there.

skills.name: Intercepts & zeros
skills.wrong_turn: A zero is an x-value where the output is 0, not the output at x = 0. That's the y-intercept.
skills.rule: The y-intercept is f(0). The zeros are the x with f(x)=0, the x-intercepts.

skills.name: Maxima & minima
skills.wrong_turn: The maximum is the height, not the location. For −(x − 2)² + 5, the max is 5, reached at x = 2.
skills.rule: A relative max is higher than everything nearby; the absolute max is highest of all.

skills.name: Piecewise functions
skills.wrong_turn: Use only the piece whose condition fits. For f(2) above, 2 is in x ≥ 2, so use 5 − x.
skills.rule: A piecewise function uses different formulas on different parts of the domain.

skills.name: Step functions
skills.wrong_turn: Floor of a negative goes down, away from zero: ⌊−1.5⌋ = −2, not −1.
skills.rule: ⌊x⌋ rounds down to an integer; ⌈x⌉ rounds up.

skills.name: Absolute value function
skills.wrong_turn: y = |x − 3| moves the V right to x = 3, not left. The vertex is where the inside is 0.
skills.rule: |x|=x for x≥0 and |x|=−x for x<0: a V with vertex at the origin.

skills.name: Combining functions
skills.wrong_turn: (f/g)(x) needs g(x) ≠ 0 even if the fraction later cancels: x²/x is not defined at 0.

skills.name: Composition
skills.wrong_turn: f(g(x)) is not f(x)·g(x). Put g's whole output inside f.

skills.name: Inverse functions

steps.b: swap x and y and solve

skills.wrong_turn: f⁻¹(x) is not 1/f(x). For f(x) = 2x, the inverse is x/2, not 1/(2x).
skills.rule: f−1 undoes f: f−1(f(x))=x and f(f−1(x))=x.
